evidence.text: Cause: the testing repository's pre-commit hook runs its whole 751-test suite on every commit, including Night Shift's history commit, and one test with a 5 second timeout is load-sensitive; it timed out on a cold first run. The shell was a coincidence and Night Shift calls git the same way from either shell. Recorded on TASK-37 as a limitation with a workaround: commit the history later with git commit --only -- .night-shift/history (hooks still run), or let the Adopter's hook skip tests when only .night-shift/ is staged. Not verified: that the original failure in the real repository was this same timeout, since its output was not captured.

feedback.title: A failed history commit keeps only the hook's last line
feedback.body: When a repository's pre-commit hook fails the history commit, the tool reports only the last line of git's output (for example 'husky - pre-commit script failed (code 1)'). The reason (which test failed, a timeout) is lost, so finding the cause meant reproducing the commit by hand with the full output captured. Keeping the last lines of the hook's output, or saving it to a file in the night folder, would make the cause visible at once.
